items.title: Don Alias interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 6, 2002
items.q: he’s one guy that I would go to lengths to do anything for.

ctx.x: Mmm, yeah, I can’t handle this kind of stuff man. And vice versa. I learned, him being there during that period of time was like he saved my spirit. He saved my spirit, which at one particular time I didn’t think was going to make it. But him being there, he’s one guy that I would go to lengths to do anything for. I’ll give you an example. If Rick called up now and said “hey man I need you up here,” I’d go without even thinking about it.
Glad to hear that. Well I learned a lot from him too actually. So I think in one respect, you must have taught me a few things through him.

items.title: Rick Montalbano interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, August 12, 2011
items.q: especially becoming friends with some of the people in the band — Don Alias in particular

ctx.x: And you were working on the music and you know, I felt really happy for you. Was that a good experience? © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -10-

That was a great experience. That was a wonderful experience, especially becoming friends with some of the people in the band — Don Alias in particular. So I highly recommend, of course our friend is gone now, but the idea of going on the road with Don Alias, more so actually than Lou Rawls, it was thrilling to me. And every day was a thrill really, because we played every day. He and I played every day. Virtually every day, aside from travel days.
You mean the two of you?
